title: Reliable frames over a lossy simulated link
objective: Implement a scoped reliable sender and receiver over a simulated datagram that drops a configured fraction of packets, transfer 10 KiB byte-identical, and show at least one retransmission in a sequence/ACK capture.
whyThisMatters: Industrial telemetry dies on links that drop. CS144's reliable byte stream is the right idea; you will implement a sliver of it (stop-and-wait or go-back-N) so later MQTT and Modbus work is not 'the library retried for me.'
evidence: A loss config file stating the drop fraction (at least 20 percent) and whether reorder is enabled
Sender/receiver C (or C plus a thin harness) with incremental Git history
A captured transfer of at least 10 KiB that is byte-identical (checksum or diff) under that loss
A sequence/ACK log showing at least one retransmission of a named sequence number
README naming which CS144 idea was used (reliable byte stream, sequence space, retransmission timer) and one CS144 topic deliberately omitted (for example congestion control)
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The lossy link drops at least 20 percent of datagrams as configured in a file the run reads; that file is in the repository.
A 10 KiB or larger payload arrives byte-identical on the receiver under that loss; a checksum or diff is captured.
The sequence/ACK log contains at least one line that shows a retransmission (same sequence number sent more than once, or an ACK gap followed by a resend).
README names at least one CS144 reliable-transport idea that was implemented and one that was omitted.
